newsitem.title: USA: Four charged in death benefits scheme.
newsitem.headline: Four charged in death benefits scheme.

text.p: Four defendants were charged Monday for allegedly running a $50 million scheme to defraud investors in a company that allegedly bought life insurance death benefits from terminally-ill policy holders.

Federal prosecutors said the four defendants were charged in a complaint filed in Manhattan federal court alleging that they fraudulently induced more than 950 investors to extend loans to PCO Inc., doing business as Personal Choice Opportunities Inc. PCO's principal offices are in Palm Springs, Calif.
Prosecutors alleged that PCO's purported business was making "viatical settlements" with terminally-ill individuals.

In a typical viatical settlement, a terminally-ill person sells the death benefits payable under his life insurance policy to an investor at a purchase price substantially lower than the benefits payable under the policy.
This allows the insured individual to obtain funds to use during the remainder of his life. When the policy holder dies, the investor collects the insurance benefits and earns a profit.
The complaint alleged that investors were induced to "lend" funds to PCO to finance the viatical settlements. The investors were promised annual interest payments of 25 percent.

Investors also were told that their funds would be held by Escrow Plus Inc., until PCO delivered assignments of group life insurance policies to be held as collateral for the loans, and that insurance benefits would be paid directly to Escrow Plus and then disbursed to the investors.
The complaint alleged that no insurance benefits have been paid into the investors' escrow accounts.

The defendants are: David Laing, 52, of Palm Springs, Calif., president and owner of PCO; Valerie Jenkins, 43, of Burbank, Calif., president of Escrow Plus; Dennis Rinner, 40, of Okemos, Mich., former PCO broker and Michael Smith, 33, of Aruro, Colo., a former PCO broker.
